newsitem.title: RUSSIA: T-bill auction fails to boost rouble.
newsitem.headline: T-bill auction fails to boost rouble.

text.p: The rouble eased on Tuesday, but dealers said it had been higher in early trading on disappointment over active demand for funds before the government bond auctions.
On December 4, the central bank will auction 8.5 trillion roubles of new six-month paper and an additional tranche of 2.5 trillion roubles of OFZ bonds.
roubles/dollar Dec 3 midday Dec 3 early Dec 2 close
Demand for the bills themselves is likely to be keen, as the central bank announced last week it was cutting the guaranteed yield for non-residents from Thursday to 13 percent from 16 percent.
But that failed to translate into increased demand for roubles, even though the currency usually firms in the run-up to the weekly auctions.

"Banks kept free rouble funds, thinking demand would be higher ahead of the auctions. But it was not so, and they decided not to sit on them. The market is high (dollar-wise) and calm now," one dealer said.
Neftekhimbank dealer Vladimir Zrazhevsky said overnight rates had not eased much on demand from small banks, while some major operators were seen buying dollars.
"But otherwise, this (dollar) buying is not a major trend," he added.
